Verified all 295 invoices (2023-2026) against tagged payments: 292 close to the exact cent, only the 3 already-known open invoices (00049971, 00050035, 00052693) have zero payment tagged, zero invoices show a partial or overpaid mismatch against payments. Follow-up: checked credit notes specifically (isolated from payments) - do CN amounts always net to zero against their tagged invoice? Answer: no. Of 148 invoices carrying at least one CN: 129 self-cancel exactly (no payment needed), 14 are partial with the remainder closed by a payment (verified: all 14 close to the exact cent once combined - normal, not an irregularity), and 5 are OVER-credited (CN exceeds the tagged invoice's amount): 00033750 (R598 over), 00036139 (R598 over), 00045078 (R517.50 over), 00047421 (R1,207.50 over), 00048980 (R1,207.50 over). Sibling-candidate search (+/-7 days, matching amount) found a confident explanation for exactly one: 00047421's CN (R3,622.50) exactly matches same-day sibling invoice 00047430 (same reference text DN#21133-EMPTY) - ASSERTED probable INVNO transposition between adjacent same-day documents, not proven (47430 itself separately closes exactly via a different CN+payment, so cash nets out fine either way - this is a document-attribution issue, not a cash-accounting one). The other 4 (33750, 36139, 45078, 48980) have no comparably strong nearby match - reported unresolved rather than force-fit. None of this affects the PROVEN R2,052.39 total balance - INVNO/CN mistagging doesn't change aggregate cash totals, only which specific document a credit note is attributed to. Same class of issue as the untagged R454.09/R1,193.96 payments already found. See reports/TAN002_Credit_Note_Reconciliation_2026-09-22.md for full invoice/CN detail on all 19 partial+over cases.

Checked whether the 5 over-credited CNs relate to the untagged R454.09/R1,193.96 payments driving today's R739.87 open exposure. Total balance of the 5 CNs: sum of CN amounts -R12,040.50, sum of invoices they're tagged to R7,912.00, total over-credit (excess) R4,128.50. Tested 3 ways, no relationship found: (1) arithmetic - all 31 subset sums of the 5 over-credit amounts, and separately of the 5 full CN amounts, checked against 454.09 and 739.87, zero matches; (2) coincidental balance landing - running balance immediately after each of the 5 CNs (R11,252.66/R695.52/R15,906.08/-R3,386.95/-R5,247.68), none near either figure; (3) timing - closest CN to the 06/03/2026 blank payment is 37 days earlier (28/01/2026), others 127-612 days earlier. Mechanically ruled out too: the one explained mistagging case (47421/47430) shows a mistagged CN still nets out fully within its own document cluster (the correct invoice 47430 closed exactly via a different CN+payment) - mistagged CNs are self-contained and cannot leak cash into a later unrelated period, unlike a genuinely untagged (blank INVNO) payment. CONCLUSION: two separate, unrelated data-quality issues in the same account - CN mistagging (Jul 2024-Jan 2026, self-contained, zero net effect) and the untagged-payment gap (Mar-Apr 2026, the actual and only driver of today's R739.87).
